text:
Alex: Heads up — I'm about to land a Terraform change that splits the secret-sync Role into two: secret-sync-cluster and secret-sync-namespace. Main reason: least-privilege for ExternalSecrets. Can folks scan? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
Maria: quick q — how will this affect the ExternalSecrets controller SA? Are we changing serviceAccountName or ClusterRoleBindings?
Alex: Good q. Plan is: create namespace-scoped Role + RoleBinding (secret-read) and a ClusterRole for listing/watch across namespaces for sync controller. We'll keep controller's SA the same but bind both where applicable. terraform snippet:
```
resource "kubernetes_role" "extsecret_ns" { ... }
resource "kubernetes_cluster_role" "extsecret_cluster" { ... }
```
Sam: two things: Vault auth role currently restricts by serviceAccountName and namespace. Splitting RBAC won't change SA name, so Vault role still fine. But if we start running per-namespace controller replicas with different SAs, that'll break.
Alex: Not planning per-namespace SA yet. However I found an edge-case when Vault Agent sidecar runs in the same pod: the projected SA token TTL was 1h and Vault k8s-auth expects audience "vault". On older clusters token projection might not be enabled. Error:
```
vault-agent: token-exchange failed: invalid token
```
Jordan: We should enable BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume for the controller SA, and add `automountServiceAccountToken: false` to any app pods that are mounting token accidentally. That prevents kubelets from giving long-lived tokens.
Priya: Are we using projected tokens today in the Helm chart? I thought the Vault injector uses `serviceAccountToken` projection via annotation `vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-template`.
Alex: Helm chart patch I'm proposing adds:
```
serviceAccount:
  create: false
  name: extsecrets-controller
podAnnotations:
  vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
  vault.hashicorp.com/role: "extsecrets-controller"
```
and in Deployment spec set
```
automountServiceAccountToken: false
```
for non-inject pods (e.g., apps) we explicitly set to false.
Maria: to be safe, we should add a pre-apply plan check that runs a k8s api check for `BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume` feature — but that's alpha in <1.20? Which k8s version do we run in prod? 1.24.
Sam: 1.24 supports projected tokens fine. Also need to ensure RBAC for token reviewer is present: system:serviceaccount:kube-system:default? No, token reviewer is ClusterRole `system:auth-delegator` binding.
Alex: I've added a terraform resource to bind `system:auth-delegator` for the extsecrets SA in our module — snippet in PR.
Jordan: pinging @DevOps Bot to run terraform plan for the PR
DevOps Bot: CI pipeline triggered: infra/terraform plan for branch secrets-rbac-split — plan succeeded with 3 additions, 2 modifications. Link: https://ci.internal/1234
Priya: anything else for rotation? My concern is secret rotation hooks that rely on being able to update Secrets — namespace Role must include `update` and `patch`.
Alex: yes added `get,list,watch,create,update,patch,delete` on secrets in Role.
Maria: LGTM, left small comment on the PR asking to add a note in CHANGELOG about vault role audience requirement.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Jordan: I'll queue a canary after deploy. If Vault auth fails we'll roll back.
Alex: thanks all — will merge after addressing Maria's comment. Will follow up with a post-deploy check list.
